content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors an encryption network for pre-trained neural networks by eliminating the effects of confusion neurons in the network and recover the original network.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths::
Motivation to prune such research is strong and should be given importance due to an increase in AIaaS.

Weaknesses:
The paper can be improved based on the following points:
1) In the introduction section, it mentions that consumers/customers can use other's AI based IPs for prediction/classification purposes. This is now called AI as a Service (AIaaS). It would be good to mention this along with proper citation.
2) In the text, it is not evident what is the computational complexity of confusion neurons? One of the motivations mentioned in section 1 is that decrypting traditional encrypted networks are computationally expensive. Comparatively how inexpensive are including confusion neurone to achieve IP verification of neural networks? Please specify this. Please also justify the design choices.
3) Experimental section (section 4) is lacking comparative study with existing traditional works in the domain such as using watermark and encryption based neural networks. Please provide results on this matter to show the efficacy of the proposed method.
4)) There are several grammatical errors. Please rectify them. For example, "θ is the parameters" should be "θ can be denoted as the parameters."
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper could be written better as pointed out in the Weaknesses section of the review for added clarity. Novelty of the proposed method is lacking, especially comparative study with existing traditional work is missing to show efficacy of the proposed.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This work considers the following threat model:
* The defender has a model running on a device that the defender does not control
* The attacker has complete control over the device and wants to obtain the weights for the model running on the device

The authors present a solution in which they add "confusion" neurons to the model that degrade accuracy and pass along an encrypted encoding of where the confusion neurons are. This way, the hope is that the attacker (a) cannot meaningfully recover the weights without the confusion neuron encoding and (b) the defender can run the model by decrypting the encoding and removing the confusion neurons from inference passes.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The approach is novel. However, the presented threat model is not well-motivated, and the method is outperformed by simple baselines in scenarios where the method is applicable.

Threat model: 
* The authors do not motivate with real world scenarios that match the given threat model. The rationale given by the paper is that an attacker could "copy the model from memory" (introduction, page 1) - if this is true, what prevents the attacker from also copying the decrypted confusion neuron information from memory?
* One scenario in which this method might have a place is when a defender wants to distribute a model publicly, and then only give the key to certain trusted parties. However, in this case encrypting the model seems strictly better. The only downside (as noted in the paper) of encrypting the whole model is that model parameters can be large in file size; but even decrypting a model only results in a 2x storage footprint compared to the original model size. This kind of space footprint is not so bad when the (very) largest models we have are all smaller than 100GB (and when the models distributed to devices for inference are usually much much smaller). Furthermore, some encryption protocols even allow for "in place" decrypting.
content.summary_of_the_review: The presented method is novel, but the motivation for the presented threat model is not strong enough.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an encryption mechanism for pretrained models. By adding a set of confusion neurons into the pretrained models, such models are free from illegal copy. They also show that the proposed approach is robust against fine-tuning attack.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
+) The paper proposes an interesting pespective for privacy protection by integrating confusion neurons into the pre-trained models.

Cons: 
-) Abstract is not clear enough to summarize the key contributions. E.g. too short and does not provide adequate information, e.g., why "the position of these neurons is encoded into a few integers that are easy to be encrypted"? Authors are not precise in their expressions, where words like "most often" and "somewhat" should not appear in technical papers. 
-) Lack of comparisons of SOTA methods. e.g. comparisons with Xue et al., 2021 Cai et al,. 2019 and Lin et al. 2021 regarding the efficiency and effectiveness are missing. 
-) What does "the well designed architecture of the model remains unprotected" mean, since the architecture is unmodified yet only the number of neurons are changed.
-) No discussion is made on the security issue of the proposed method as how to defend against potential attacks other than fine-tuning. For example, the attacker can estimate the number of poisonous neurons by analyzing the inference time, and then decrypt the model by collision attack. After all, compared to previous methods which encodes nearly all neurons, simply adding poisonous neurons while exposing the exact neurons can be very dangerous. Fine-tuning is only among the worst effectiveness among potential attacks.
-) Typos are here and there. Authors should thoroughly polish this paper. I just list a few in the follows, P1 "make the encrypted model cannot be used",  "A secret key that records". I do not think this work meet the requirement of ICLR in such a terse presentation.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
-) Not clear written
-) Limited novelty and quality
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes an encryption mechanism for pretrained models. By adding a set of confusion neurons into the pretrained models, such models are free from illegal copy. However, the paper has limited novelty on designing an encrpytion scheme for privacy protection of deep pretrained networks, based on 1) lack of comparison of SOTA methods and 2) missing experiments on other attacks (e.g. collision attack).

content.title: An Encryption Framework for Pre-Trained Neural Networks
content.abstract: Having consumed huge amounts of training data and computational resource, large-scale pre-trained models are often considered key assets of AI service providers. This raises an important problem:  how to prevent these models from being maliciously copied when they are running on customer's computing device? We answer this question by adding a set of  confusion neurons into the pre-trained model, where the position of these neurons is encoded into a few integers that are easy to be encrypted. We find that most often, a small portion of confusion neurons are able to effectively contaminate the pre-trained model. Thereafter, we extend our study to a bigger picture that the customers may develop algorithms to eliminate the effect of confusion neurons and recover the original network, and we show that our simple approach is somewhat capable of defending itself against the fine-tuning attack.
